findings.text: follow-on (regression, reproduced): batching writes a second source row keyed to the pre-reboot boot, and _consumed_whole_and_untouched selects an arbitrary one of them, so a single receipts file that spans a reboot is never recognised as consumed-whole and its whole consumed region is re-digested on every ingest pass forever. A file spanning a reboot now commits once per boot key (host, boot_id, path, inode), leaving the pre-reboot row at its batch-boundary offset (< size) and the post-reboot row at the end; _consumed_whole_and_untouched (telemetry_index.py:916-925) queries 'WHERE path = ? AND inode = ?' with fetchone and no ORDER BY, which returns the earlier-inserted pre-reboot row whose offset < size, so the method returns False. Reproduced on this node in a scratch copy of the reviewed head: a 4-row file with two rows under boot_before and two under boot_after, ingested with batch_rows=2, leaves source rows [('3f8a1c2e-...', 842, 1684), ('7d2e4f60-...', 1684, 1684)] and _consumed_whole_and_untouched(source) == False with sample_count 4. At the base revision the same file wrote a single source row at the final boot with offset == size, so this fast path fired; the change costs the whole-record re-read the method's own docstring exists to avoid (measured there at 8.6 s a pass over 49 sources and 220 MB). Correctness is unaffected (resume uses _resumed_row ORDER BY offset DESC, which picks the post-reboot row; samples carry their own boot_id), so this is a performance regression on a narrow trigger, not a wrong answer.

follow-on (receipt fidelity): the gate log's second command line records 'pytest tests/test_agent_serve_registry.py -k agent_pytest_v2 2>/dev/null' with the summary '1 passed, 8 deselected' (line 9), but -k agent_pytest_v2 selects no test: 'pytest --collect-only -q tests/test_agent_serve_registry.py -k agent_pytest_v2' reports 'no tests collected (9 deselected)'. The done-when selector is agent_package_modules_parse_with_serving_python (which collects test_agent_package_modules_parse_with_serving_python, 1 of 9), and the manifest's own tests line names it, so the summary beside the logged command can only have come from the done-when selector, not the one written. The guard itself is sound -- run independently at the reviewed head it passes (1 passed, 8 deselected, EXIT=0), and the node's 97-passed first arm is reproduced exactly (97 passed, EXIT=0) -- but the gate receipt does not record the command that actually ran.

follow-on (control quality): the recorded negative control -- 'setting the batch size to one row must fail the commit-count test' -- does not name what it mutated, and the test it targets hardcodes its own boundary (index.ingest([source], batch_rows=250)), so setting the module default DEFAULT_BATCH_ROWS to one row would leave that test green; the red log can only have been produced by editing the test's argument (a test-input mutation) or by editing the production comparison. The check is nevertheless effective on production: forcing per-row commits in the production loop (since_commit >= 1) reddens the same test with '1000 commits for 1000 rows', and the node's own log already shows the correct red (AssertionError: 1000 commits for 1000 rows, EXIT=1). Recorded so a later reader knows the control was not a mutation of the module constant the manifest's wording implies.

item_verdicts.diff: read the reviewed diff 4516e26e..6bbea311 in the reviewed worktree -- imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py (+286/-104 effectively 380 insertions / 104 deletions across three files), tests/test_telemetry_index.py (3 new tests), and the evidence fragment. The change is exactly the declared one: _insert stops opening a transaction per row, ingest accumulates DEFAULT_BATCH_ROWS (1000) lines and commits them together with a source row that advances offset, size, mtime and prefix digest to the batch's last line via the new _record_source, an uncommitted batch is rolled back on raise, and _resume now returns a digest object seeded with the already-consumed prefix so the caller reads off the region digest at any line boundary. The sample uniqueness (host, boot_id, inode, offset) and the source upsert key (host, boot_id, path, inode) are unchanged; the only new behaviour beyond the goal is the reboot-spanning source-row split, recorded as a finding.

item_verdicts.goal: read the goal ('Commit the telemetry ingest in bounded batches instead of once per row') against the code and the measure -- the ingest no longer commits per row, it commits in bounded batches whose boundary is a resume point, and the cost is measured: cold ingest of a 20 MB / 31,888-line receipts cut is 169.937 s at base 4516e26e against 2.979 s at head 27ab3e34 (~57x), both arms reporting 31,888 rows stored. The mechanism is correct on inspection (batch end = offset + len(raw) with raw newline-terminated matches tail, and the incremental digest reaches sha256 of the prefix), and the two new tests assert the commit count through sqlite3's own set_trace_callback and the digest against the file's own sha256. The goal is met; the reboot-spanning fast-path regression is a side effect outside the goal, recorded as a finding.

justifications.durability: the mechanism is durable: the boundary is the byte after the batch's last newline, the source row advances with the samples in one transaction so a kill resumes at the last committed batch and re-reads nothing, and the digest is extended incrementally to the same whole-region identity an unbatched pass records -- all three asserted by committed tests (commit count via set_trace_callback, resume-after-kill with zero duplicates, prefix_sha == file sha256). Docked to 16 because the change silently disables an existing durability-of-cost guard: a file spanning a reboot is no longer recognised as consumed-whole (reproduced), so the fast path its own docstring documents stops firing for exactly the multi-boot case the module asserts elsewhere.
justifications.evidence: reproduced independently rather than accepted: base arm 94 passed EXIT=0 and head arm 97 passed EXIT=0 (the three new tests), the serving-interpreter guard 1 passed EXIT=0 at both arms, ruff clean at both arms, giving added_failure_count 0 -- derived from this review's own arms because the reviewed run was dispatched unarmed; the negative control is red for the right reason (1000 commits for 1000 rows, EXIT=1) and forcing per-row commits in production reddens the same test; the measure artifact is internally consistent (offset arithmetic and digest identity verified by reading the code). Docked to 17 for the gate receipt: gate.log:7 records a selector (-k agent_pytest_v2) that collects no test, contradicting the summary on the line beside it.
justifications.fit: the change reads in the file's own idiom -- _record_source carries a docstring in the same voice as its siblings, the batch boundary reuses the existing tail arithmetic, the rollback restores the pre-existing no-half-written-state property, and the naming checks over the changed paths return no plan, ticket or version labels (DEFAULT_BATCH_ROWS and batch_rows name the capability). The commit messages are conventional, carry bodies, and cite no plan or ticket identifiers. Docked to 18 only for the loose commit-body parenthetical describing the assertion as '(>1 and <=6' where the test asserts non-empty and <=6.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the goal is achieved and the implementation correct: commits are batched at a module-constant default with a test keyword, the source row advances per batch so a mid-source kill resumes at the last committed batch with no committed row re-read, the digest is byte-region identical to an unbatched pass, and the whole thing is measured at ~57x on the fleet allocation without changing the sample-uniqueness or deselected-tier behaviour the spec requires be preserved. Docked one square because the batching changes an unrequested behaviour -- a single file spanning a reboot now yields two source rows where before it yielded one -- and although that split matches the module's own stated invariant, it is what defeats the consumed-whole fast path (finding 1).
justifications.scope_discipline: the reviewed node's writes are confined to the two declared source paths, the evidence fragment and the run report directory; no plan, sprint, shared index or out-of-scope file is touched, the fragment is committed inside the head commit rather than left in the worktree, and no figure was written when the done-when names none. Nothing beyond scope was edited, so 20.
